page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-4GB is a budget-oriented virtual server based on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor. The configuration includes 2 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, with 2 physical cores and 1 thread per core. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate that this server operates in the lower performance tiers. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core and multi-core stress-ng scores, both placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10%, though small-block cached reads perform slightly better in the bottom 25%. Geekbench testing shows average single-core performance and text processing, but multi-core operations, software compilation, and image processing remain in the bottom 25%. Database operations, such as Redis SET and PassMark database tests, also show weak to poor throughput.

Given its shared CPU model and modest memory capacity, this server offers a resource-dense, entry-level hardware profile suitable for low-intensity workloads. The tradeoff of shared CPU resources makes it less suitable for sustained high-performance computing or heavy database tasks. It is best utilized for basic web serving, lightweight text processing, small-scale development environments, or running minor background utilities where high CPU availability is not continuously required.
